articles.title: Jovem é atacado com facão no pescoço enquanto dormia em Roraima | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima conseguiu fugir após cair no chão e foi levada para um hospital. O crime ocorreu na manhã deste domingo (20), em Caracaraí
articles.summary: Vítima conseguiu fugir após cair no chão e foi levada para um hospital. O crime ocorreu neste domingo (20), em Caracaraí.
articles.body:
Vítima foi transferida para o Hospital Geral de Roraima (HGR), em Boa Vista. — Foto: João Gabriel Leitão/g1 RR/Arquivo

Um jovem, de 21 anos, ficou ferido após ter a casa invadida por três homens e ser atacado com um golpe de facão no pescoço enquanto dormia , na manhã deste domingo (20), em Caracaraí , no Sul de Roraima. Ninguém foi preso.

O crime ocorreu por volta das 9h, no bairro Livramento. O jovem contou à Polícia Militar que os três suspeitos arrombaram a porta da casa e, em seguida, o atacaram com o facão. Após ser atingido, ele caiu no chão, mas conseguiu se levantar e fugir do local.

O jovem conhecia os suspeitos e contou à PM que a confusão começou na noite de sábado (19), quando ele, o pai e os três homens estavam em um bar. Segundo a vítima, houve uma discussão por causa de uma mulher que se relacionava com o pai dele e com um dos envolvidos.

Ainda de acordo com a vítima, durante a discussão, ele entrou em luta corporal com um dos homens para defender o pai. Depois da briga, segundo o relato, o suspeito voltou ao local com uma arma de fogo e tentou atirar contra o jovem.

Após o episódio, o jovem e o pai voltaram para casa. Na manhã deste domingo, os três homens o atacaram.

Ele foi atendido pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e levado para um hospital. Segundo a PM, o jovem estava sem risco de morte e aguardava transferência para o Hospital Geral de Roraima (HGR), em Boa Vista .

A polícia fez buscas na região, mas os suspeitos não foram encontrados. O caso foi registrado na delegacia como tentativa de homicídio qualificado .

articles.title: Hythe family shares hidden cost of cancer after teen's diagnosis
articles.summary: Maya, 13, from Hythe in Kent, was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when she was three.
articles.body:
The parents of a teenage girl with a rare form of childhood cancer say the hidden costs of caring for their daughter have left them in fear of losing their home.

Maya, 13, from Hythe in Kent, was diagnosed with neuroblastoma at three years old, but relapsed in 2023 having been in remission for five years.

Her mother, Dellanie, said the pressure of paying a mortgage and bills whilst she and her husband, Terry, are working less to care for Maya is continuing to take its toll on their family of five.

Dellanie, an NHS nurse, said: "Whilst your child is poorly and you are fighting for her life, the bills don't stop coming."

She added: "My husband has lost his income as he is caring for Maya, and these days you need two people working just to keep your head above water.

"It has been very, very difficult but our aim has always been to to look after our child as well as each other.

"I always put a brave face on - of course I'm hurting, but I can't be in the corner crying."

Maya, who her mother described as a "larger than life person" who loves animals and music, was first diagnosed with neuroblastoma near her adrenal gland when she was three-years-old.

Neuroblastoma is a rare cancer which mainly affects children under five-years-old and around 100 children are diagnosed with it a year in the UK, according to Cancer Research UK.

After initially going into remission, Maya's neuroblastoma returned three years ago, and has since been cared for by specialist teams including at the Royal Marsden hospital in London, and Great Ormond Street Hospital.

In 2025, during a clinical trial of CAR T-cell therapy, a technique currently used to treat some types of leukaemia and lymphoma, Maya developed a brain injury which Dellanie said left her "profoundly disabled".

Her disability meant Terry had to leave his job to care for Maya full time, while Dellanie reduced her working hours to care for her, and support her husband.

Dellanie said: "I just have to be grateful for what we have got.

"At the moment, Maya is a fighter and there is so much fight in her."

Charity Young Lives vs Cancer says families of children with cancer face average extra costs of around £700 a month, and an average loss of income of about £6,000 per household.

Sonia Malik, the charity's associate policy director, said: "We find people are having to dip into savings, and most of these costs are immediate.

"It impacts the whole family and their lives are thrown into chaos.

"The financial stress should be the last thing families have to think about."

Malik said that some support is available for cancer patients and their carers, such as financial support from charities, disability benefits and carer's allowance, but it can take time for families to receive benefits support.

articles.title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan’s sister arrested before planned PTI march
articles.summary: Khan’s party condemns his sister’s arrest as an illegal attempt to silence her over PTI leader’s ongoing imprisonment.
articles.body:
Pakistan’s police have arrested Aleema Khan, the sister of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, from her house in the eastern city of Lahore, the capital of Punjab province.

The arrest on Sunday came exactly a week before a planned protest march by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on September 27 to demand his release .

A senior police official in Lahore, requesting anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media, confirmed the arrest but did not give more details.

The deputy commissioner of Lahore passed an order, a copy of which was seen by Al Jazeera, for Aleema Khan’s 30-day detention under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) law of Punjab.

The law allows the authorities to order the preventive detention of a person if deemed necessary for public order or safety.

“Aleema Khan left her home in the morning with the driver when the police illegally arrested her and took her to an unknown location,” her lawyer Rana Mudassar Umer said in a post on X.

“Aleema Khan has bail in all her cases in Lahore. It is not yet known in which case, location, or police station she is being held.”

There was no immediate comment from the government on the arrest.

On Saturday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi ⁠said the government would do ⁠everything it could to ⁠stop the PTI protest march, the Reuters news agency reported on Sunday.

The PTI condemned the arrest, calling it illegal and demanding her immediate release.

“This is not law. This is an illegal arrest. This is cowardice and a deliberate attempt to worsen the situation,” PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram posted on X.

“An elderly lady, the sister of an imprisoned former prime minister, has been illegally arrested from her doorstep because she refused to stay silent about her brother’s illegal detention, solitary confinement, and denial of medical care,” he added about the woman in her 70s.

Imran Khan, 73, has been jailed since August 2023 over a series of convictions his party calls politically driven. All but one have since been suspended or overturned on appeal.

Concerns over his health, in particular the condition of his right eye , which has required months of specialist treatment, have driven the PTI campaign to demand his release.

His sons – Sulaiman and Kasim Khan – told Al Jazeera recently that they are increasingly worried after hearing that their father is “agitated” and suffering from “severe anxiety”.

Last month, the country’s Supreme Court ordered Pakistani authorities to transfer the former prime minister to the privately-run Shifa International Hospital in the capital, Islamabad.

Under the order, Khan was to remain there under medical care until the case was next heard, according to his lawyer.

Officials instead took him to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) for a brief check-up before returning him to jail and did not give him access to his personal physician, which his party says was a breach of the top court’s orders.

articles.title: Sorority rush gets Ozempic makeover as some college women resort to weight-loss injections
articles.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy are said to be quietly reshaping sorority rush culture, as college students chase an increasingly thin beauty ideal.
articles.body: As GLP-1 medications continue to surge in popularity for weight loss and diabetes treatment, their use is rising among younger adults — with anecdotal reports suggesting the trend is making its way onto college campuses. Market research has shown that GLP-1s – including semaglutide (Ozempic and Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro and Zepbound) – are growing fastest among adults under 40, particularly young women. A 2024 analysis published in JAMA found that 162,439 young adults ages 18 to 25 received at least one dispensed GLP-1 prescription in 2023. Women accounted for 76.4% of those patients, although the analysis included medications prescribed for both diabetes and weight management. PATIENTS TAKING WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS OFTEN MAKE 5 CRITICAL MISTAKES, DOCTOR WARNS Separately, the 2025 Monitoring the Future survey found that 2% of students in grades 8, 10 and 12 reported using a prescription GLP-1 medication, while another 2% said they had used one without a prescription. A recent feature in The Cut, "The Secret 'Ozempidemic' on Sorority Row," argues that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs have quietly become part of campus culture at some elite universities, particularly within the competitive sorority recruitment process. Three female students interviewed under pseudonyms said they were using compounded semaglutide or tirzepatide to improve their chances during rush and to meet an increasingly thin beauty ideal. The students described a pressure to look extremely thin, noting that social media and weight-loss competitions among friends have fueled increased GLP-1 use. POPULAR GLP-1 WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DEADLY BRAIN DISORDER "For many young women who have just arrived on campus, thinness feels like the ticket into the best possible college experience," one student said. "I didn't realize that someone who was 19 and also not super-overweight could get on it. I was like, ‘I gotta hop on,’" another said. One former sorority recruiter said, "It's like, 'Well, there's no excuse for people to be fat because they could just get a GLP-1.'" ‘Cosmetic shortcut’ Jay Campbell, longevity and peptide expert and bestselling author, said that while these drugs were built to solve a metabolic crisis, they've been "hijacked as a cosmetic shortcut." "For someone who's metabolically dysregulated, they are a genuine medical intervention," he told Fox News Digital. "But to a 20-year-old sorority member with a normal BMI, they look like an aesthetic hack in a syringe." "Sororities are built on social visibility and constant comparison," Campbell said. "Everyone is looking at everyone's Instagram." "When one girl drops 15 pounds in six weeks, that news spreads through the sorority house faster than any diet fad in history, because the results are fast, dramatic, and don't require the discipline of nutrition or training." "When one girl drops 15 pounds in six weeks, that news spreads through the sorority house faster than any diet fad in history." College-aged women already tend to have "high body-image sensitivity," he noted, which is heightened in the age of "a full-scale social contagion." OZEMPIC USERS MAY BE MAKING A MAJOR WEIGHT-LOSS MISTAKE, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS "Many of these young women grew up already fighting disordered relationships with food and their physical bodies, and [now] you have a medication that can play on their insecurities." That’s not to say GLP-1s don’t benefit many patients. In clinical studies of people taking the medications for obesity, fat mass generally accounts for more of the lost weight than lean mass, Campbell pointed out. "The peptide isn't catabolic by itself – the real risk is that a healthy 20-year-old who isn't obese has far less metabolic and muscular reserve to lose from in the first place." When a young woman loses weight rapidly without consuming enough protein or doing resistance training, she may lose a greater proportion of lean mass, Campbell warned. Rapid weight loss can also contribute to the facial or body changes sometimes referred to as "Ozempic face" and "Ozempic body." 5 steps college students should take before starting a GLP-1 For college students considering a weight-loss medication, Campbell recommends taking the following five steps before beginning treatment. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES No. 1: Know whether the medication is medically appropriate "If you're not obese or metabolically compromised, ask yourself honestly why you're taking a medication designed for a disease you don't have," Campbell suggested. No. 2: Protect muscle during weight loss While muscle loss is preventable, it requires work that most people using these drugs for cosmetic reasons aren't doing, Campbell said. "That means real protein intake, not a protein bar as an afterthought, and resistance training," he advised. "Skip both, and you will absolutely lose muscle tissue that you cannot easily get back at 20 years old." While adequate protein intake and resistance training may help reduce muscle loss, the amount of lean mass lost varies from person to person. No. 3: Understand fertility considerations "Fertility matters here in a way most college students never think about," Campbell said. GLP-1 medications should not be used for weight loss during pregnancy, experts agree. Semaglutide labeling advises stopping Wegovy at least two months before a planned pregnancy. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Tirzepatide has been shown to reduce the effectiveness of oral hormonal contraceptives during treatment initiation and dose increases, so the FDA advises using an alternate method for four weeks during those periods. No. 4: Discuss mental health and eating behaviors Mental health still deserves attention, particularly for young adults with depression, anxiety, eating disorders or a history of using food to cope emotionally. While the FDA has found no increased risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior from GLP-1 medications, patients should tell their prescriber about any new or worsening mood symptoms. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP No. 5: Recognize the limits of long-term data "Nobody knows what 10 or 20 years of GLP-1 use looks like in a woman who started at 20 with a normal body weight, because that population barely existed in the clinical trials," Campbell cautioned. "Consider this a reminder to stop treating a powerful metabolic medication like a lifestyle accessory." While GLP-1 medications can suppress appetite, Campbell added, "they will not fix a broken metabolic foundation or whatever underlying reason a 20-year-old feels she needs to lose weight in the first place." "We’ve built a pharmaceutical shortcut that used to require months of behavior change, and young women in high-visibility social environments are early adopters of anything that changes how they look, fast." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Campbell stressed that treatment should involve a qualified prescriber who evaluates the patient’s medical history and goals, provides appropriate monitoring, adjusts the dose as needed and helps manage potential side effects. articles.title: Kolkata shocker: Bedridden man bludgeoned to death by brother over property dispute
articles.summary: Bedridden Teghoria man Balaram Rajbanshi was bludgeoned to death in Baguiati; brother Krishna arrested, allegedly staged robbery over property dispute.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A 28-year-old bedridden man was found bludgeoned to death at his home around noon on Sunday. The house too was found ransacked with gold ornaments and other costly items, worth Rs 1.5 lakh, missing from the almirahs.Cops said the victim’s elder brother has been arrested for murdering the 28-year-old following a property dispute and desperation over the victim — bedridden since 2017 after an accident — ‘hurtling the family into a financial crisis following repeated surgeries’. “He then threw away items around the room to make it look like a robbery,” an officer said.The victim has been identified as Balaram Rajbanshi, who underwent a brain surgery a few days ago. The incident was reported from near the Charigram Sri Ramkrishna Ashram Adarsha Balika Vidyalaya in Raghunathpur area of Teghoria under Baguiati PS.Police said that around 12.50 pm, Balaram was found lying in a pool of blood on his bed with severe injuries on his forehead. Cops said he was found unconscious on his bed by his mother who had just returned from work. “He had reportedly been bedridden following a surgery. Police immediately reached the spot. The room was found open, the almirahs unlocked, and clothes and other articles scattered on the floor. A lacerated injury was noticed on the deceased’s scalp,” said cops.“During probe, we found that his elder brother, Krishna Rajbanshi (33), had murdered him over a property dispute and attempted to portray the incident as theft. The accused has confessed to have committed the crime. He will be produced in a court on Monday with a prayer for police custody,” said a senior officer of Bidhannagar Police. The body has been sent to R G Kar Medical College and Hospital for post-mortem.According to police and family, the incident occurred between 8 am and noon. Balaram, who could barely recognise family members and communicate with them, was alone at home alongside their pet dog, a mongrel, after his family members left for their daily work in the morning. The victim’s mother works as a domestic help, while his father runs a fish trade. His brother, the accused Krishna, worked as a food delivery agent.The family was trying to complete the construction of their two-storey house. While the first floor was nearing completion, money constraints stopped the work on the first floor. articles.summary: Bengaluru: Intruder entered Peenya home via first-floor window, choked 29-year-old with dupatta, stole 50g gold chain and Rs 30,000; suspect detained.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A 29-year-old homemaker stepped out of her bathroom to a nightmare when an intruder grabbed her from behind and choked her with a dupatta after entering her Peenya 2nd Stage home through a first-floor window.She lost consciousness during the attack and, on recovering, found her 50-gram gold mangalya chain, worth around Rs 5 lakh, was missing.The miscreant also broke open a wardrobe and took away Rs 30,000 in cash.According to a complaint filed by Kavya (name changed), the incident occurred around 12.30pm on Sept 17, when she was home alone as her husband, a private firm employee, had gone to attend a housewarming ceremony of their relative and their five-year-old daughter was at school.After finishing the house chores, Kavya wanted to take a bath. She said she went to the ground floor of the house and locked all the doors and windows. Then she went to the first floor of the house and locked the door from inside before going to the bathroom to bathe. She had left a window next to the door slightly open.Soon after finishing her bath, she stepped out of the bathroom.The woman said she was grabbed from behind by an unidentified man. He asked her not to make noise or retort and said he would leave after taking whatever he wanted from the house.Kavya said the attacker squeezed her neck with his hands. When she was finding it difficult to breathe, the miscreant took a dupatta and wrapped it around her neck, tightening and twisting it while again warning her not to scream.Kavya told police that she lost consciousness. articles.summary: Chennai: Alleged stalker Jaishankar died after being hit with an iron rod at a woman’s Alapakkam home; police arrested two and changed the case to murder.
articles.body: CHENNAI: A 38-year-old welder, who had allegedly been stalking a woman and asking her to continue their relationship, died at Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital on Saturday after he was beaten with an iron rod following a quarrel at the woman’s house in Alapakkam. Police altered the case from attempt to murder to murder.Police identified the deceased as Jaishankar, a resident of Mudichur Road in West Tambaram. Police said he installed a gate at Poongodi’s house, 45, Kesavaraya Mudali Street, Alapakkam, about four months ago. The two subsequently became acquainted and remained in touch over the phone.Police said Poongodi blocked Jaishankar’s phone number about 10 days ago. Jaishankar went to her house and argued with her over the issue.Poongodi informed her acquaintance Damodaran, 33, about the quarrel. Damodaran arrived and asked Jaishankar to leave. When the argument continued, Damodaran picked up an iron rod from the house and struck Jaishankar on the head, critically injuring him.Hearing his cries, neighbors rushed him to the Government District Headquarters Hospital in Tambaram and later shifted him to the Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital for further treatment.Peerkankaranai police registered a case and arrested Damodaran and Poongodi. articles.title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
articles.summary: Massage flu symptoms like soreness, fatigue and headaches are real, but experts debunk the popular claim that massages release toxins from the body.
articles.body: A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches. Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness. The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis. DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH "This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital. "The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently." Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added. "Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said. Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover." "The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media." A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments. "This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this." Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes. To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Voelsch also suggested drinking water, eating something light beforehand and moving gently afterward. Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor. "If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Voelsch recommended seeking medical advice if symptoms last longer than about 72 hours or include fever, sharp or radiating pain, numbness or tingling, spreading swelling or bruising, or faintness.

articles.title: Justiça determina criação de Centro de Parto Normal em Imperatriz para atender gestantes de baixo risco | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura e Estado do Maranhão devem criar estrutura provisória em até 20 dias; multa diária é de R$ 5 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: Prefeitura e Estado do Maranhão devem criar estrutura provisória em até 20 dias; multa diária é de R$ 5 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
A Justiça determinou que a Prefeitura de Imperatriz e o Estado do Maranhão adotem medidas urgentes para reorganizar o atendimento obstétrico na região. Entre as principais determinações estão a implantação de um Centro de Parto Normal (CPN) para gestantes de baixo risco, a criação de uma estrutura provisória em até 20 dias e o pagamento de multa diária de R$ 5 mil em caso de descumprimento.

A decisão é da 2ª Vara da Fazenda Pública de Imperatriz e foi tomada após a Justiça identificar sobrecarga na Maternidade de Alto Risco de Imperatriz (MARI) e falta de uma unidade municipal voltada a partos de baixo risco

Entre as gestantes de Imperatriz atendidas na unidade, cerca de 69,4% foram classificadas como de risco habitual, ou seja, casos de baixa complexidade que, segundo a decisão, poderiam ser acompanhados em unidades específicas para esse tipo de atendimento.

A Justiça considerou que a concentração desses casos na MARI contribui para a sobrecarga da unidade e reduz a capacidade de atendimento de pacientes que precisam de assistência de maior complexidade.

Além da demanda de Imperatriz, a MARI recebe pacientes de outros municípios da região e também de estados vizinhos, como Tocantins e Pará.

Diante do cenário, a Justiça determinou que a Prefeitura de Imperatriz adote as providências necessárias para implantar e colocar em funcionamento um Centro de Parto Normal (CPN), destinado ao atendimento de gestantes de baixo risco pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

O município terá até 30 dias para apresentar um plano técnico-operacional detalhado. O documento deverá informar, entre outros pontos, o local de funcionamento, estrutura disponível, adequações necessárias, cronograma de implantação, orçamento, fontes de custeio, composição das equipes e capacidade de atendimento.

O Estado do Maranhão também deverá, no mesmo prazo, informar de que forma o futuro centro será integrado à rede estadual de atenção obstétrica e neonatal e quais medidas de cooperação serão adotadas.

Estrutura provisória deve funcionar em até 20 dias

Enquanto a solução definitiva não for implantada, Estado e Município deverão colocar em funcionamento, em até 20 dias, um Centro de Parto Normal provisório nas dependências do Hospital Regional de Imperatriz (HRT) ou em uma estrutura acoplada.

A unidade temporária será destinada exclusivamente ao atendimento de gestantes de baixo risco e deverá contar com equipe própria, equipamentos, insumos e medicamentos necessários ao funcionamento.

A estrutura provisória deverá permanecer em operação até a implantação definitiva do serviço municipal, por um período máximo de 180 dias.

A Justiça também determinou a implantação de um sistema de monitoramento diário da MARI, com informações sobre número de pacientes, cirurgias realizadas, salas em funcionamento, ocupação de leitos e tempo de espera para procedimentos obstétricos urgentes. Em caso de descumprimento, foi fixada multa diária de R$ 5 mil, inicialmente limitada a 60 dias.

Em nota enviada à TV Mirante , a Secretaria de Estado da Saúde informou que ainda não havia sido notificada da decisão e que, quando isso ocorrer, adotará as medidas cabíveis. A pasta também afirmou que a Maternidade de Alto Risco de Imperatriz passou recentemente por uma reestruturação.

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de Imperatriz, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportage

articles.title: Ônibus invade rodoviária de Campinas e deixa dois feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo da Viação Piracicabana atingiu uma pilastra ao chegar ao terminal na noite de domingo (20); vítimas foram socorridas ao Hospital Mário Gatti.
articles.summary: Vítimas do acidente na rodoviária de Campinas foram levadas ao Hospital Mário Gatti após ônibus da Viação Piracicabana atingir pilastra no terminal.
articles.body:
Duas pessoas ficaram feridas após o motorista de um ônibus perder o controle, bater em uma pilastra e invadir a área de embarque e desembarque do Terminal Metropolitano Rodoviário de Campinas (SP), na noite de domingo (20).

Em nota, a administração da rodoviária informou que o acidente aconteceu por volta das 21h20, quando o ônibus da Viação Piracicabana chegava ao terminal.

O terminal informou que ninguém se feriu no acidente. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, no entanto, duas vítimas precisaram ser socorridas e foram levadas ao Hospital Mário Gatti , mas não há informações sobre o estado de saúde delas.

Imagens recebidas pela EPTV mostraram que a porta do veículo ficou amassada. Os vidros da lateral também foram quebrados para permitir a saída dos passageiros.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e isolou a área para auxiliar no atendimento às vítimas. Duas viaturas do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) também estiveram no local.

Apesar do acidente, as demais operações da rodoviária seguiram normalmente. A EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, entrou em contato com a empresa Viação Piracicabana, mas não recebeu retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Avó desmaia ao ver o neto pela primeira vez em maternidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Menino nasceu em um hospital da Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre. Antes do parto, pais do bebê chegaram a ficar presos no elevador da unidade de saúde por cerca de 30 minutos.
articles.summary: Menino nasceu em um hospital da Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre. Antes do parto, pais do bebê chegaram a ficar presos no elevador da unidade de saúde por cerca de 30 minutos
articles.body:
Uma avó desmaiou de emoção ao ver o neto pela primeira vez na maternidade de um hospital de Novo Hamburgo , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre . A reação de Márcia Maria Scaratti Bley, de 58 anos, foi gravada pelo fotógrafo Leonardo Link e viralizou nas redes sociais.

Bernardo Farias Bley nasceu na madrugada de 9 de agosto, Dia dos Pais. Com 35 semanas de gestação, a chegada antecipada do menino surpreendeu os pais, Fábio Gabriel Bley, 32, e Taís Mara Farias Bley, 29.

"Minha mãe acabou desmaiando devido a muita emoção. É o primeiro neto dela que foi muito aguardado", conta Fábio.

A chegada do casal ao Hospital Regina, por volta das 2h da madrugada, já foi marcada por um susto: o elevador travou e eles ficaram cerca de 30 minutos presos , até que uma equipe de manutenção chegou para retirá-los.

"Ao fechar a porta ele travou e não respondia a nenhum comando, entramos em pânico", conta o pai.

Ele conseguiu contato com o cunhado e ligou para a equipe de manutenção, que enviou um técnico. Em seguida, a gestante foi atendida e encaminhada para a cesárea.

Em nota, o hospital afirma que "mãe e filho não tiveram nenhuma intercorrência e receberam alta médica na manhã do dia 11 de agosto de 2026 em ótimo estado de saúde". Leia a íntegra abaixo.

Quando receberam a ligação de que o neto estava a caminho, os avós, que moram em Rolante , a cerca de 60 km do filho, correram para o hospital. "Nem sei que roupa eu botei. Eu sei que quando eu cheguei no hospital, eu estava com uma meia de cada cor", afirma Márcia.

O bebê nasceu saudável, às 6h42, e logo pôde ser apresentado à família pelo vidro do berçário . Foi nesse momento, quando avistou o neto no colo do filho, que Márcia, arrebatada pelo sentimento, foi ao chão . Apesar do susto, a equipe a socorreu e ela logo retornou ao vidro para admirar o pequeno.

"Escureceu e eu não vi mais nada, sabe? Eu fiquei três dias com 'galo' na cabeça", conta.

Ela tem diabetes e pressão alta, o que acredita que possa ter contribuído para o mal estar.

Agora, o vídeo fica como recordação para a família, que pretende mostrá-lo ao menino quando ele crescer. "Vamos guardar para mais tarde mostrar pro Bernardo rir junto", conclui a avó.

Avó desmaia ao ver o neto pela primeira vez em maternidade no RS — Foto: Imagens cedidas/Leonardo Link

"O Hospital Regina informa que, na madrugada do dia 9 de agosto de 2026, foi registrada falha no elevador de acesso ao Centro Obstétrico, situação que foi prontamente solucionada e não impactou na condução do atendimento.

A paciente passou pela triagem no Hospital Regina às 2h20 desta data, quando recebeu a classificação verde, o que representa um atendimento pouco urgente. O nascimento do bebê ocorreu pouco mais de 4 horas depois, às 6h42.

Mãe e filho não tiveram nenhuma intercorrência e receberam alta médica na manhã do dia 11 de agosto de 2026 em ótimo estado de saúde."

articles.title: Homem é preso após agredir companheira e esfaquear avó na Serra | G1
articles.standfirst: Casal estava separado há um mês. Alisson da Silva Prates fazia ameaças de morte à esposa.
articles.summary: Homem preso na Serra invadiu a casa da família e atacou as vítimas após um mês de separação; a idosa foi levada ao hospital Jayme Santos Neves.
articles.body:
Um homem foi preso na noite deste domingo (20) após agredir a esposa e esfaquear a avó dela no bairro Cidade Nova da Serra , na Serra, Grande Vitória.

O pedreiro Alisson da Silva Prates, de 35 anos, invadiu a casa onde a família morava e fez ameaças de morte. Não há informações do estado de saúde da vítima.

Segundo a Polícia Militar, a mulher estava separada de Alisson há um mês. De acordo com o relato dela, ele era alcoólatra e, quando bebia, a agredia verbalmente em casa. Ela já havia solicitado medida protetiva contra ele na quinta (17) e no sábado (19).

Ainda segundo a mulher, a avó dela estava dormindo na hora do crime. Ele invadiu a casa fazendo ameaças de morte para a mulher, que fugiu pela janela para escapar do agressor.

Alisson da Silva Prates foi preso por agredir a companheira e a avó ela na Serra, Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo Pessoal

A avó foi atingida com facada sno tórax e socorrida por uma ambulância da Ecovias Capixaba e levada para o Hospital Jayme Santos Neves, na Serra.

Alisson se entregou à polícia ainda no local do crime e mostrou aos policiais onde estava a faca usada por ele. O homem foi levado para a Delegacia Regional da Serra. Ele afirmou ainda que queria ter agredido mais as mulheres.

O g1 procurou a Polícia Civil para saber qual foi a autuação de Alisson, mas não houve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Hospital é condenado após paciente ficar 4h30 molhada de urina em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher relatou que vazamento de sonda encharcou cama e chegou até a altura do pescoço. Justiça fixou indenização de R$ 15 mil.
articles.summary: Justiça de MS condena hospital a pagar R$ 15 mil por negligência após paciente ficar horas molhada de urina devido a falha em sonda cirúrgica.
articles.body:
Caso foi julgado no Tribunal de Justiça em Campo Grande — Foto: Divulgação/TJMS

Uma mulher que havia acabado de passar por uma cirurgia relatou ter ficado cerca de quatro horas e meia molhada de urina após uma sonda apresentar vazamento em um hospital de Campo Grande . A unidade foi condenada a pagar R$ 15 mil por danos morais.

Segundo o processo, o problema começou logo após ela ser levada para o quarto. A cama ficou molhada e, conforme o relato da mulher, a urina chegou até a altura do pescoço. Sem conseguir se locomover sozinha por causa da cirurgia, ela e familiares pediram ajuda à equipe de enfermagem.

Uma técnica identificou o problema no dispositivo, mas, de acordo com a ação, não fez a troca por falta de autorização da enfermeira responsável. A sonda foi substituída cerca de quatro horas e meia depois.

A mulher afirmou ainda que a urina atingiu a malha cirúrgica usada no procedimento, que precisou ser trocada antes do previsto. Na ação, relatou sofrimento físico, constrangimento, angústia e preocupação com o risco de infecção.

O hospital alegou que a colocação da sonda era responsabilidade do médico cirurgião e que não havia registro de falha da equipe de enfermagem no prontuário. Também afirmou que o tempo de espera era justificável pelos protocolos de classificação de risco.

A perícia realizada durante o processo não identificou sequelas permanentes, mas apontou que o vazamento de uma sonda vesical exige intervenção imediata.

Para o juiz Juliano Rodrigues Valentim, da 3ª Vara Cível de Campo Grande, o caso não poderia ser tratado como uma intercorrência comum do pós-operatório, já que o problema foi comunicado à equipe e exigia providência rápida.

A sentença também destacou que protocolos internos e classificação de risco não afastam o dever de prestar cuidados básicos e contínuos.

O magistrado rejeitou ainda o argumento de que a responsabilidade caberia ao cirurgião. Segundo a decisão, o problema ocorreu durante a manutenção e o manejo da sonda no pós-operatório, atividade ligada à assistência de enfermagem.

articles.title: Homem preso no HUT por ameaçar policial civil em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Mandado de prisão foi cumprido no hospital, ele foi submetido ao procedimento e posteriormente será encaminhado ao presídio. Outro homem suspeito dos mesmos crimes também foi preso. Conforme o delegado Laércio Evangelista, do Draco, ambos integravam uma facção criminosa.
articles.summary: Homem preso no HUT integrava facção criminosa e fazia ameaças contra investigador por redes sociais mesmo internado após sofrer acidente de trânsito.
articles.body:
Um homem, que não teve seu nome informado, foi preso nesta segunda-feira (21) ao dar entrada no centro cirúrgico do Hospital de Urgência de Teresina , suspeito de ameaçar policiais civis da cidade de Nazária, cidade a 30 km da capital. Além dele, outro homem foi preso pelos mesmos crimes.

A prisão aconteceu em cumprimento de mandado de prisão pelo Departamento de Repressão a Ações Criminosas Organizadas (Draco), da Polícia Civil do Piauí.

Conforme o delegado Laércio Evangelista, coordenador do Draco, ambos integravam uma facção criminosa. O homem que foi preso no hospital havia se envolvido em um acidente de trânsito e foi preso quando dava entrada no centro cirúrgico.

"Cumprimos dois mandados de busca e duas prisões. Um deles estava nas dependências do HUT por ter se envolvido em um acidente de trânsito e demos cumprimento ao mandado no momento em que ele ia para o centro cirúrgico. Inclusive na data de ontem [19], ele já internado no hospital e continuava mandando ameaças pelo celular", disse o delegado.

HUT Teresina — Foto: Lucas Marreiros - g1

De acordo com a polícia, após uma série de operações realizadas em Nazária, Demerval Lobão e por equipes da própria Draco, integrantes do Bonde dos 40 passaram a intimidar o investigador responsável pelo cumprimento dos mandados, além de outros policiais. As ameaças eram feitas por meio de redes sociais e aplicativos de mensagem, como WhatsApp e Instagram, com o envio de áudios e imagens de conteúdo intimidatório.

O homem preso no hospital, conforme o delegado, tinha passagens anteriores pela polícia e é apontado como uma liderança ligada à disciplina interna da facção, o que a polícia chama de atuação em "tribunais do crime", ou seja, punições e assassinatos.

O coordenador do Draco informou ainda que as ações de repressão ao crime organizado serão intensificadas em Nazária e cidades vizinhas, e que ameaças contra agentes de segurança pública não serão toleradas. Ele afirmou que a polícia vai continuar monitorando a atuação de integrantes da facção na região.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Russia to test Nato pact' and 'Labour eye tax raid'
articles.summary: Potential threats from Russia to Nato and speculation over Labour's tax plans ahead of the Budget lead Monday's papers.
articles.body:
The Guardian reports that European intelligence officials have raised the possibility of an imminent test of Nato by Russia , quoting one official as saying an attack could come in a matter of "months not years". The paper says the escalation fears come as the UN General Assembly convenes in New York later this week, and amid intensifying airstrikes on both sides of Russia's war on Ukraine.

The lead for the Sun is its own investigation made in conjunction with Channel 5 into the murder convictions of the neo-natal nurse Lucy Letby, who was found guilty of killing seven babies and attempting to kill seven more. The paper says it has spoken to a "top consultant" who worked alongside her, who claims that she may have been a scapegoat to cover up for failings at the Countess of Chester Hospital. One mother tells the paper that her baby died six months after Letby had been moved off the neo-natal unit.

The Times says it's carried out analysis which shows that more than half of Labour MPs in England and Wales have a higher number of people claiming disability benefit in their constituencies than the size of their majorities. The paper says the figures highlight what it calls the "political peril" facing ministers trying to cut the welfare bill.

Labour is considering raising Capital Gains Tax to help fund an increase to the income tax personal allowance, according to the Daily Telegraph. It says the idea has come from the Labour donor Dale Vince, who has warned the party that wealth is being "taxed more lightly than work". The paper also quotes the green energy entrepreneur as saying that the move would give "millions of people a meaningful boost" - with the biggest benefit going to those on the lowest incomes.

The Daily Mail reports that Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch would ditch what it's calling a "tourist tax " which visitors to the UK have to pay on goods. The paper says she is pledging to bring back the VAT-free shopping initiative which was axed by her party in 2021. Speaking to the Mail, Badenoch said Britain should be a "magnet" for tourists who want to spend.

The paper also carries comments from Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who has said intelligence reports suggest it would be part of Moscow's efforts to test whether Article 5 - which holds that Nato members will come to the defence of an ally under attack - is "more theoretical than practical".

articles.title: Teenager Megan Hilton saves five lives through organ donation
articles.summary: The 17-year old from Liverpool donated six organs after her death following a brain aneurysm.
articles.body:
A teenager who hoped to become a nurse helped save five lives by donating her organs after her death.

Megan Hilton, from Liverpool, was 17 when she died after suffering a brain aneurysm in July 2025.

She had joined the NHS Organ Donor Register and spoken to her family about her wishes, which her father said meant they "knew exactly what Megan wanted" when they were told she would not survive. In total, she donated six of her organs.

The family said they wanted to share her story during Organ Donation Week to encourage other people to sign up and help save lives.

Megan was studying Health and Social Care at Hugh Baird College and hoped to become a children's nurse.

She volunteered at Liverpool Women's Hospital and completed work placements at Aintree University Hospital, where she developed an interest in neonatal and paediatric nursing.

Her father, David Hilton, said: "Megan was always thinking about other people. She wanted to help wherever she could and she was determined that, if anything happened to her, she wanted to be an organ donor."

He said discussing her wishes helped the family when they were told she was not going to survive.

"Having that conversation to fall back on made an impossible situation just a little bit easier," he said.

"By donating her organs, Megan saved five lives. She never got the chance to become a nurse, but she still helped people in the most extraordinary way."

NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) has warned of a "sharp" decline in organ donation, with deceased donation rates 9% lower than at the same point last year.

It said 8,700 people were waiting for a transplant and had launched an "urgent response plan" after family consent rates fell from 67% in 2020-21 to 57% last year.

Laura Winn-Jones, a specialist organ donation nurse, said Megan's story showed "the incredible difference one person can make" and encouraged people to talk to their families about their organ donation decisions.

Organ Donation Week runs from 21 to 27 September.

University Hospitals of Liverpool Group said buildings across its hospitals would be illuminated pink during the week to raise awareness of organ donation and honour donors and their families.

Megan's family hopes sharing her story will encourage more people to make their organ donation wishes known and discuss them with their loved ones.

articles.title: Meet Natalie Groeger, the woman turning 101: Her simple daily habits include staying active, eating in moderation, staying positive and making time for family and friends
articles.summary: Wellness News: At 100, Natalie Groeger still starts her mornings with a small ritual that has little to do with expensive wellness routines. She gets dressed in some.
articles.body: At 100, Natalie Groeger still starts her mornings with a small ritual that has little to do with expensive wellness routines. She gets dressed in something she likes, puts on a little makeup and begins her day feeling good about herself.This October, Groeger will turn 101. Looking back on more than a century of life, she says her formula has been surprisingly ordinary: keep moving, watch what you eat, stay positive, laugh often and make time for people.There is no single food or miracle routine on her list. Instead, Groeger believes that the way she approaches everyday life has helped keep her feeling young.Meet Natalie GroegerGroeger, who previously worked as a switchboard operator and customer service representative, is now the matriarch of a four-generation family. She has two children, four granddaughters and six great-grandchildren.She celebrated her 100th birthday in 2025 with more than 80 relatives, friends and members of the team at The Bristal at Englewood in New Jersey, where she lives.Her 101st birthday celebration will be smaller, but she says the people around her remain the most important part of the occasion.“Being together with my family is what matters most to me,” Groeger told PEOPLE.She kept moving for most of her lifePhysical activity has been another constant.Groeger says she danced and walked every day until about the last year. She now puts less emphasis on the amount of exercise and more on the importance of having remained physically active for much of her life.Her approach also reflects something researchers have repeatedly observed about healthy ageing: longevity is influenced by a combination of factors rather than one magic habit. Physical activity, diet, social relationships and psychological wellbeing can all play a role in how people age.Her diet is about moderation, not restrictionGroeger does not describe herself as someone who completely avoids indulgent foods.“I let myself indulge, but I try not to overdo it,” she told PEOPLE.That small detail may be one of the most relatable parts of her longevity philosophy. Rather than presenting a highly restrictive diet, she describes paying attention to what she eats while allowing herself some indulgence.The habit she believes matters mostFor Groeger, however, longevity is not just about food or exercise.She says maintaining a “lighthearted spirit” and a positive attitude keeps her young. She also makes an effort to smile, laugh and have conversations with people around her.“I don’t stress about things that I can’t control,” she said, adding that people should enjoy the moments they are given each day and keep finding reasons to smile.Her social connections remain strong even when family members cannot visit in person. Groeger regularly video chats with her four granddaughters and six great-grandchildren between visits.What makes her happiest nowAfter 100 years, Groeger says her greatest source of happiness is not a particular health habit at all. It is seeing what came after her.She takes pride in watching her children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren build their own lives and describes herself as proud of the legacy her family represents.For her 101st birthday, that seems to be exactly what she wants more of: time with the people she loves.Her story does not offer a guaranteed recipe for reaching 100. Instead, it offers a glimpse into how one centenarian has chosen to live her days: keep moving when possible, eat with moderation, take care of yourself, stay connected and, perhaps most importantly, find something to smile about.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Fitness expert reveals 6 things people over 35 should do after workouts to stay strong
articles.summary: Fitness coach Jacob Zemer shares six post-workout recovery strategies for adults over 35, from sleep and heat therapy to protein and stretching tips.
articles.body: The most important part of a workout may happen after it ends. As adults age, muscles can become less responsive to protein and other muscle-building signals, making post-exercise recovery critical for repairing tissue and preserving strength. Jacob Zemer, a New York-based fitness coach, focuses heavily on recovery with his clients, who primarily range from 35 to 55 years old. ONE MUSCLE PROTEIN MAY HOLD THE KEY TO STAYING STRONGER AS YOU AGE, STUDY FINDS "Most of my clients are really focused on longevity," he told Fox News Digital. "They're not people who are looking to be bodybuilders or power lifters – they want to age well." Zemer shared the following six ways adults over 35 can recover more effectively after exercise. No. 1: Get enough quality sleep "Getting seven to nine hours of quality sleep is vital," Zemer told Fox News Digital. COMMON BEDROOM MISTAKE COULD BE QUIETLY TAKING A TOLL ON YOUR HEALTH, EXPERTS SAY He suggested the following steps to support deeper, more restorative sleep. No. 2: Get regular bloodwork Getting regular checkups and completing recommended lab work can also help identify issues that may interfere with recovery, according to Zemer. "Make sure you’re keeping up with what's going on with your hormones," he advised. "Make sure everything in your body is functioning properly, because as we age, our bodies change." 3 COMMON FACTORS MAY BE SECRETLY SPEEDING UP THE AGING PROCESS, EXPERT SAYS Experts emphasize, however, that preventive testing should be personalized based on factors such as age, gender, symptoms and medical history. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends screening for conditions including high blood pressure, prediabetes/type 2 diabetes and osteoporosis. No. 3: Use warmth to support recovery Heat exposure may be another way to support muscle strength and recovery after exercise, Zemer suggested. Warmth causes blood vessels to widen, increasing circulation to tired muscles and potentially helping to deliver nutrients involved in repair. A 2025 review of 22 studies found that nearly half of participants reported improved muscle-function recovery with heat therapy. "If you don't have access to a sauna, taking a hot shower after your workout releases heat proteins that may help with recovery – and actually it helps improve what we call ‘gains’ from the gym," the trainer told Fox News Digital. No. 4: Stretch "After you get done working out, your muscles are shortened," Zemer said. "And so you want to re-lengthen them by stretching." As strength training can put significant wear and tear on the body, it’s important to maintain full mobility by moving through a complete range of motion and stretching afterward, according to the expert. No. 5: Fuel and hydrate Getting adequate protein after a workout to aid in muscle repair and rebuilding, Zemer emphasized. The International Society of Sports Nutrition recommends targeting about 20 to 40 grams of high-quality protein after training. For active adults, the general guideline is roughly 1.4 to 2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Protein needs should be individualized, however, particularly for people with certain medical conditions. Hydration is also important prior to working out, Zemer added. "If you don't drink enough water, you're really setting yourself up for failure when you're in the session, which is going to cause you to have lackluster results," he said. No. 6: Give your body time to de-stress "You just did something that, even if it’s healthy and has a positive impact on your body, still stresses your body," Zemer said. "Your cortisol’s high. So getting a good meal and a little bit of rest before you move on with your day" can help the body recover. "If it takes you a full week to recover, you simply trained too hard." The goal is to give the nervous system and muscles the resources they need to recover. A 2026 review described exercise as a cycle of "stress response, adaptation and recovery," noting that the benefits of workouts depend on sufficient recovery time, sleep and energy availability. The difference between ‘good sore’ and ‘bad sore’ While it’s normal and generally a good thing to feel sore after exercise, Zemer said there’s a fine line between "good" and "bad" soreness. "The soreness should be only for a short period of time, like maybe a day or so after you're done training," he told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "If it takes you a full week to recover, you simply trained too hard." Zemer noted that the body adapts to training gradually, so people should ease into a new fitness routine rather than pushing too hard too soon. "If you have extended amounts of soreness that exceed two or three days, you did too much," he said. "If your knees and joints ache, you did too much." That doesn’t mean it’s necessary to stop working out, however. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "It just means maybe drop back what you did by 30% and start from there," Zemer advised. "For example, if you did six sets of legs, try instead to do four sets of legs the next time you train. That's going to make it far more effective for your recovery." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The most important thing to recognize, according to the trainer, is that exercise-induced endorphins can temporarily mask pain. Discomfort that seems manageable during a workout may feel worse later, once those chemicals wear off. "If something hurts in the gym when you have your endorphins going strong, it's going to hurt really bad later – and that's the last thing you want, because if you're hurt, you're not going to be able to train consistently."

articles.title: If Trump wants to lower drug prices, his obvious free-riding targets are outside the US
articles.summary: President Donald Trump secured nine drug pricing deals, but lasting relief requires pressuring foreign countries to pay their fair share for medicine.
articles.body: President Donald Trump just secured nine new pricing agreements with drug manufacturers that could help reduce what Americans pay for many prescription medicines. The deals demonstrate Trump's commitment to lowering drug prices for patients. The president's dedication – and his desire to negotiate with companies individually, rather than imposing broad mandates – is commendable. But his efforts would be better directed at the root cause of high drug prices: foreign countries free-riding on American drug innovation. To deliver lasting price reductions while protecting U.S. leadership in biomedical innovation, the Trump administration must focus its negotiating strategy overseas – and intensify its push to make other countries pay their fair share for the medicines America develops. TRUMP EXPANDS TRUMPRX PRESCRIPTION DRUG DISCOUNT PROGRAM TO MORE THAN 800 MEDICATIONS For decades, wealthy foreign governments have used price controls, mandatory rebates, reimbursement delays and other policies to suppress what they pay for innovative medicines. These measures allow foreign countries to reap the benefits of new treatments while forcing Americans to bear a disproportionate share of the cost of developing them. American patients currently account for roughly three-quarters of pharmaceutical profits and over half of global research and development spending – far more than America's share of the world economy. If U.S. leaders want to correct this imbalance, putting more pressure on drugmakers isn't the solution. Instead, the administration must focus on getting other countries to end their free-riding practices. Forcing U.S. prices lower without increasing foreign countries' contributions risks harming both American patients and our broader biotech industry. Some members of Congress, for example, have proposed writing "most-favored-nation" drug pricing into law – permanently tying U.S. drug prices to the artificially low prices paid abroad. ROBERT F KENNEDY JR: THE FUTURE OF MEDICINE SHOULD BE BUILT IN AMERICA Such an approach would effectively import foreign price controls into America – reducing funding for future research and development and slowing the development of new treatments. It could also threaten jobs, undermine manufacturing investment and weaken U.S. drugmakers' ability to compete with China. To sustain both lower prices and continued innovation here at home, other wealthy countries will need to step up and shoulder more of the costs. 3 STEPS THAT COULD STOP FRAUD AND MAKE HEALTHCARE MORE AFFORDABLE FOR ALL AMERICANS Fortunately, the Trump administration's negotiating skills offer a way to make that happen. The same hard-charging approach it has used to negotiate recent deals with manufacturers can also be applied abroad to pressure foreign governments to reform their pricing policies. The United Kingdom is a clear example. Last year, Trump negotiated a deal that will require Britain to increase what it pays for new medicines by 25%. As Britain contributes more toward developing new medicines, the cost burden on the United States will decrease. MARK CUBAN SHOOTS DOWN PRESIDENTIAL BID AS HE TEAMS UP WITH TRUMP ADMIN TO CUT HEALTHCARE COSTS The administration is also laying the groundwork for a similar agreement with Germany. In June, it launched a formal investigation into how Germany's drug price controls have harmed American commerce. This investigation will give American trade officials the leverage they need to negotiate fairer pricing policies and practices with German policymakers. For decades, wealthy foreign governments have used price controls, mandatory rebates, reimbursement delays and other policies to suppress what they pay for innovative medicines. The next step should be to apply this strategy to other wealthy nations. Countries like Japan, France and Switzerland use tactics similar to Germany's to pay far less than fair value for new drugs. In Japan, for example, roughly half of newly launched medicines are subject to annual price cuts. INNOVATION IS KEY TO AMERICA STAYING A SUPERPOWER. BUT IT IS MISSING AN ESSENTIAL PIECE According to one analysis, if other developed countries all paid U.S. prices for new prescription drugs, global pharmaceutical revenue would rise by more than $254 billion. That would provide a major influx of revenue for American drug innovators – potentially fueling a research and development boom that would create jobs across the country while delivering more and cheaper lifesaving treatments for patients.
